shared_elements: standing stone monolith carved in low relief
row of repeated arch/crescent (U-shaped) motifs across the upper zone
horizontal band or belt-like register crossing the shaft
circular disc set at the centre of the shaft
paired arms/limbs rendered as curving relief lines converging toward the centre
incised parallel lines forming a band of pattern
justification: The most specific correspondence is the shared vertical scheme: a row of repeated arch-like motifs across the top, below which curving arm-like reliefs descend toward a central circular disc set on a horizontal belt-like band, all on a broad upright block. The biggest difference is in execution and subject — A is dark, smoothly polished with shallow, abstracted, sunken forms, while B is pale, coarser stone bearing crisply modelled, recognisably naturalistic animals (quadruped, bird, snake-like forms) with no counterpart in A's abstract vocabulary.
